newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Yantian to list 116 mln A shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Yantian to list 116 mln A shares.

text.p: China's Shenzhen Yantian Harbour Co Ltd said on Thursday it would list 116 million domestic currency A shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange next Monday.

The firm, which operates port facilities in Shenzhen's Yantian harbour northeast of Hong Kong, made an initial public offering (IPO) of 125 million A shares priced at 5.31 yuan each earlier this month, it said.

The rest of the A shares are held by the company's staff, which will be floated after the 116 million A shares are listed for six months, the company said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Prior to the IPO, the company had a total of 460 million non-tradeable institutional shares held by the state-owned Yantian Harbour Group.
Net proceeds of 647 million yuan from the IPO would be used to fund construction of two bulk cargo berths and a 74,000-square-metre marine container storage area, Yantian Co has said.
Yantian Group has a HK$3 billion marine container handling venture, Yantian International, with Hong Kong's Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, Yantian Co has said.
The group has a 27 percent stake in the venture, which was set up in late 1993 with registered capital of HK$2.4 billion. The Hong Kong firm holds the remaining 73 per cent.
Yantian Co posted net profits of 168 million yuan in 1996 against 159 million in 1995 based on Chinese accounting standards.
Yantian Co also owns a 66.67 percent stake in a 72-kilometre highway in China's southern province of Guangdong.
